question: What is the Angelus, and when is it traditionally prayed?

choices.A: A devotional prayer commemorating the Annunciation, traditionally prayed three times daily at 6 AM, noon, and 6 PM at the sound of the bell
choices.B: A prayer prayed only on the feast of the Annunciation (March 25)
choices.C: The opening prayer of every Mass
choices.D: A Rosary variation prayed only during Lent

teaching.title: The Angelus
teaching.body: The Angelus (from the opening words 'Angelus Domini nuntiavit Mariae' — 'The angel of the Lord declared unto Mary') is a short devotional prayer commemorating the mystery of the Incarnation through the Annunciation. It consists of three versicles with the Hail Mary and a concluding collect. Traditionally the Angelus bell rings at 6 AM, noon, and 6 PM, calling Catholics to pause and pray. During Easter season it is replaced by the Regina Caeli ('Queen of Heaven'). The practice dates to the medieval period.
